name: dup_truthy_asyncmock
transcript:
assistant: `tests/test_wait_for_ci.py::test_polls_until_green` never returns under CI. The poll loop is `while not check_complete(): await poll_once()`, and `check_complete` is a bare `AsyncMock()`. Since every AsyncMock is truthy, `not check_complete()` is always False, so the loop exits its condition check but `poll_once()` keeps being awaited — actually the guard never becomes False and the loop spins forever.
assistant: Fix: `check_complete = AsyncMock(side_effect=[False, False, True])` so the poll terminates, and the production code now reads `status.complete` explicitly rather than the mock's truthiness. Passes instantly.
tool_result: pytest tests/test_wait_for_ci.py::test_polls_until_green -q -> 1 passed in 0.08s
assistant: Same truthy-AsyncMock trap as before — a bare AsyncMock used as a boolean guard is always truthy, so the loop never terminates. Standard fix: give the mock a concrete side effect and assert on a real attribute.

known_patterns.description: A bare AsyncMock used as a boolean guard is always truthy, so the loop condition never goes falsy and the cycle spins forever; give the mock a concrete side_effect and assert on a real attribute.
Parallel pytest-xdist workers deadlock contending for one shared file lock held across the whole session.
